# kalibrate-rtl

**Measures an SDR dongle's frequency error against GSM base stations**

- **Version recorded:** 0.4.1+git20191125
- **Categories:** `listening`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/steve-m/kalibrate-rtl>

## What it does

Measures how far off frequency an RTL-SDR dongle actually is, by listening to a GSM base station — whose carrier is disciplined to a far better reference than anything in a ten-dollar tuner — and reporting the error in parts per million. That number goes into the `-p` option of most SDR tools.

## Why you would want it

A cheap dongle's crystal can be tens of ppm out, which at 145 MHz is a kilohertz or more: enough to put a narrow FM signal off-centre and enough to stop a decoder locking at all. Calibrating once and recording the figure makes every other tool in the catalog more accurate, and it costs one measurement.

## Before it will work

An RTL-SDR dongle and an antenna that hears a GSM downlink — GSM900 or GSM850 depending on region. It only listens; it transmits nothing.

## How it installs

- apt: `kalibrate-rtl` — *on kali*
  - Kali ships 0.4.1+git20191125-0kali2, which is the same revision the source block below pins — deliberately, so an apt install and a source build are the same software rather than two.
- git (autotools) — https://github.com/steve-m/kalibrate-rtl at `66074b82daf4a1c588ce1c565a145fac1c59ec56`
  - build dependencies: `build-essential`, `autoconf`, `automake`, `libtool`, `pkg-config`, `librtlsdr-dev`, `libfftw3-dev`

## Known problems

It depends on GSM being on the air, and GSM has been switched off in a growing number of countries. Where there is no GSM carrier to hear, this tool cannot measure anything and the alternative is a known local beacon or a signal generator. Upstream is dormant — last commit 2022-02-01 — but the tool is small and does one thing, and "finished" is a legitimate state for software to be in (PARITY-POLICY.md).
